sentences.text:
The allegations in brief are that the accused have illegally transported sand in a Tipper without valid permit and the permit said to be issued by Hatti Gold Mines Limited, had lapsed and the royalty was fake, wherein the registration number of the vehicle was mentioned as KA-33-B-5296.
03.

The FIR is registered on a complaint lodged by the Geologist, Department of Mines and Geology,
Yadgir.

sentences.text: Petitioner is arraigned as accused No.1 in the FIR.

04. The question that would arise in this case is as to whether the complaint lodged with the police in respect of an offence under the provisions of the KMMC Rules, 1994, is maintainable, in view of the Bar under Section 22 of the MMDR Act, 1957, which stipulates that no Court shall take cognizance of any offence except upon a complaint in writing made by a person authorized in this regard.

NC: 2024:KHC-K:9532 05. Rule - 44(1) of KMMC Rules 1994, invoked in the FIR is in respect of contravention of the provisions of Sub-Rule 1 of Rule 42 and the same is punishable under Rule - 44 (1) of the KMMC Rules 1994.

The Rules are framed exercising powers confirmed under Section 15 of the MMDR Act,
1957.

Section 22 of the said Act makes it clear that cognizance of any offence punishable under the Act or any Rules made thereunder cannot be taken except upon a complaint in writing by a person authorized in this behalf by the Central Government or the State Government.
Hence, registration of the FIR alleging violation of Rule 44 (1) of KMMC Rules is without jurisdiction.
The cognizance of the said offence cannot be taken by the jurisdictional Magistrate, if a report is filed.

06. This Court in Saiyed Jiyaulla and others vs. State of Karnataka and another in Criminal Petition No.4250/2018, disposed on 28.06.2018, has held that the police would not get any jurisdiction to register a case under Section 154 of Cr.P.C. and investigate the matter, NC: 2024:KHC-K:9532 and to file any report under Section 173 of Cr.P.C., nor the Courts have no jurisdiction to receive such reports under Section 173 of Cr.P.C. and to take cognizance for the offences punishable under Section MMDR Act, in view of the specific Bar under Section 22 of MMDR Act.

entities.text: Saiyed Jiyaulla and others vs. State of Karnataka and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 07. Insofar as the offences alleged under the provisions of the IPC are concerned, investigation cannot be curtailed.

08. In the light of the above discussion, the following;
ORDER I. Petition is partly allowed.
II. The registration of FIR in Crime No.4/2024 of Shahapur Police Station, Dist: Yadgir, under Rule 44 (1) of KMMC Rules, 1994, is hereby quashed.
III. Investigation to be continued in respect of rest of the offences registered in the FIR.
Petitioner is at liberty to challenge the final report if any filed against him.
